--- ## Working notes (internal, not for the cell) ### Pass 2 findings, 2 Sep 2026 - **The platform is dated and static.** The site's own sitemap puts every policy page at **lastmod 14 May 2026**. The only page touched since is the **/doorstep_2026 canvass form, 8 Jul 2026**. Updates and Events are both still empty. That converts every site cell from "lastmod n/a" to a real date, and it means **no new policy has been published in 111 days**. - **The accordions are empty of substance.** The Priorities page invites you to "Expand each section to view more detail." Expanded, the sections contain exactly the ten bullets already on the home page. There is no hidden second layer of platform. **The card is not missing content; the content does not exist.** - **Her quotes are campaign-issued.** The launch story states the quotes came from "a news release," so the M6 sentence is drafted campaign text, not an interview aside. That strengthens rather than weakens it. - **Six priorities at launch, three pillars on the site.** The 15 May release listed six: restoring trust and accountability; public safety and crisis response; livable neighbourhoods; responsible and affordable housing; **protecting affordability for residents and businesses**; and strengthening the local economy. The site consolidated to three pillars and **the affordability plank did not survive with any instrument attached**. That is the cleanest question to put to her. - **Her own canvass asks about taxes; her platform does not answer.** /doorstep_2026 offers voters six issues including "Taxes and spending" and "Downtown and small business." She is collecting on both and has published a position on neither. Not scoreable, but it is the sharpest gap on the file. - **Two namesakes ruled out.** X **@WendyBowkett** and the Facebook page **"Councillor Wendy Bowkett"** belong to a district councillor for the Wainfleets, **East Lindsey District Council, Lincolnshire, England**. Her real account is **@wdbowkett**. Any future verifier who sources from the other two will corrupt this file. - **Instagram correction.** An **@wdbowkett** Instagram exists but is **private**, 130 followers, personal. The earlier "no Instagram account located" line was wrong in fact and right in effect: it is not a campaign channel and yields nothing. - **Local coverage is exhausted.** A site search of Victoria News for "Bowkett" returns exactly one 2026 article and one 2011 series. Nothing on CHEK, Victoria Buzz, or Capital Daily. - **No questionnaire responses exist publicly.** The Victoria Labour Council ran a 2026 municipal questionnaire and completed endorsement interviews (page lastmod 12 Aug 2026) but publishes no responses and does not name her. No Chamber or DVBA council questionnaire with published answers was located. - **LinkedIn was not retrieved** — disallowed by robots.txt. Not worked around. ### Carried from pass 1 - **Times Colonist, still unresolved.** The 4 May 2026 commentary "A crisis of confidence in Victoria City Hall" is Cloudflare-blocked on four routes. **Authorship was never verified and nothing from it is scored.** It is the single largest open item on this file: if it is hers, it is the likeliest source of a tax, governance, or downtown mark, and the card must be re-run. - **The 518-units post is not scored.** "Our 2 sqkm neighbourhood absorbed 518 new residential units/yr for the past 5 yrs with \~5500 units in the pipeline and CityOfVictoria has failed to provide any community amenities other than 2 public toilets" is dated **12 Nov 2024**, so it is not 2026 campaign text. It is pinned on her 2026 campaign account, which is arguably an act of 2026 adoption. **Rule call for Joa, not for the verifier.** If pinning counts, it lands on M6 or M24b and n rises to 11. - **Not a source, applied:** her endorsement post for another candidate; MBA, business-strategist practice, Downtown Residents' Association leadership and Soup Kitchen board service; a 2019 letter to Council located in the City's eSCRIBE archive; the absence of any council record. - **Rows to put to the candidate before publication:** rows 3 (M7), 7 (M26b), 18 (M73d), 53 (M80c) are the four full marks and each rests on a single site bullet. Row 12 (M34–M37) is the one comparable-instrument reading on the card and is the most likely to be argued down to Partial 1.0, which would move the mean to 1.75 and leave the band unchanged. - **Actions found that contradict a 2026 sentence:** none. She held no City office 2022–26, so there are no Record lines, no incumbent cap, and the challenger rule applies: 2026 plan at face value. - **Next mandatory re-check:** after the Declaration of Candidates on **11 Sep 2026**, and immediately if /updates or /our-events publishes anything. - **M83** (civic access / public correction) has no cell in this 55. Not scored. --- ## INTERNAL proposed letter — do not publish **PROPOSE: B** (not LIVE). Joa applies the live letter; compute must not overwrite it. **Unchanged by the pass-2 sweep** — the sweep added dates, corrections and exclusions, not marks.
Item Value
Scored marks (n) 10 — rows 1, 3, 7, 12, 18, 33, 42, 49, 51, 53
Marks Aligned 3.0 ×4 · Close 2.0 ×1 · Partial 1.0 ×4 · Weak 0.5 ×1 · Opposed ×0
Sum 18.5
Mean 1.85
Band B− (1.75–1.99)
Mapped onto the live set **B**
Threshold met Yes — 10 scored answers, above the 5 required
Sensitivity Row 12 argued down to 1.0 gives mean 1.75, still B−, still B. The letter is stable against the one soft call.
**What the number is actually saying.** Four exact instrument matches out of ten answers, and forty-five unknowns. Where she names an instrument she names ours almost verbatim — Local Area Plans, a Strategic Economic Plan, tenure-priority approvals, non-police crisis response. Everywhere else she is silent, and the silence is concentrated in the three topics the framework is built on: the household bill, downtown order, and the smaller scored Hall. **The mean is high because the denominator is small, not because the platform is deep.** **What would move it.** A published tax path (M66), a household-bill number (M66d), any bylaw-hours or public-order commitment (M26/M27), or a unit and composition target (M6). Any one of those changes the letter materially; a fifth soft governance sentence would not. **The pass-2 sweep establishes that none of these will appear on their own** — the platform has not changed since 14 May and the campaign publishes nothing. They will only appear if she is asked.
